correctness.rationale: The binary-coordinate operation (1) follows by direct substitution. Its left translations independently flip exactly the Q-1 nonzero fibers. Any automorphism normalizes their generated group and hence preserves its two singleton orbits and its Q-1 two-element orbits. Conjugation gives the centralizer condition phi(u+c)=phi(u)+c, and direct substitution proves it sufficient for arbitrary eta. This determines both full groups, stabilizer orders, and the linear subgroup for every r>=2. Direct socle equation gives rank-two boundary and all larger ranks; the cycle identity and retraction follow explicitly. Standalone exhaustive tests cover every permutation in ranks 2 and 3 and all parameterized candidates at rank 4; infinite claims rest on proof, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Automorphism groups of the pointed magmas introduced in a 2026 transposition research problem are the central objects of the paper. The theorem gives a natural complete noncyclic infinite-family classification, explains exceptional nonadditive symmetries through intrinsic left-translation fibers, and quantifies large wreath-group orders, the exact additive subgroup and the rank-dependent socle/retraction. For 16 points the pointed group has order 6144 versus only 192 additive automorphisms. It is more than an arbitrary finite computation or a restatement of general retractibility.
